brief: Tonight is Legs A, and it is the same Legs A your app offered you yesterday. Nothing has been logged since Pull A on 10 September, so as far as the repo knows you have had two full days off. Read that sentence carefully, because if you actually trained last night and your phone has not synced yet, everything below is for a night that already happened — plug in and let it upload before you lift, since the moment a session I have not seen lands, this whole card expires and you drop back to the app's own numbers, which still believe the calf press is 300. Assuming you did rest: none of tonight's numbers have moved since yesterday, and that is on purpose. No new session means no new evidence, and re-deriving numbers from the same evidence just invents a different answer every morning. All three of your trainers argued it again from scratch this morning and landed on exactly the same eight prescriptions, so there is nothing for me to split. What still matters is the thing that mattered yesterday: this is the first Legs A since 20 August, twenty-three days, and the first one at the new gym. Four of tonight's lifts happen only on Legs A, so their numbers were all read on machines in the building you left on 2 September. The calf press asks 260, not 300 — on this gym's sled on 5 September you did 240, 260, then 260. The leg press opens at 140, then 180, then 200 as the work set, down from 240, because the one leg press reading you have here came in 20 pounds under the old machine for the same movement, and because you topped out at 160 on the high-foot version on 5 September. The leg extension is a blank slate — nobody has touched that machine here, not once — so take 105, then 135, and log the pin you actually use; that becomes next week's real number instead of an inherited one. The hip abductor goes to 142.5, because you closed 135 for fifteen here on 5 September and that earns the next step. Leg curl, hip adductor, cable crunch and the Bulgarians are unchanged. Two cues: on the Bulgarians, weaker leg first and match it, never beat it; on the calf press, pause at the bottom instead of bouncing. Two asks. Put your bodyweight in — the last reading is 23 August at 207, twenty days ago, and with the show on 1 March that is the one number your trainers keep having to guess at. And you have three Yes/No cards waiting from yesterday that nobody has answered yet.

flags.note: Nothing has been logged since 10 September. If you trained last night and it has not synced, sync before you lift — the moment that session lands, tonight's card expires and the app falls back to old-gym numbers.
Every number below is identical to yesterday's, deliberately. No new session was logged, so there is no new evidence, and all three trainers re-argued it this morning and agreed on all eight lifts.
First Legs A in 23 days and the first at the new gym. Six of tonight's nine lifts are machines, and every machine number the app had on its own was read at the old gym.
Left alone your calf press card would say 300. On 5 September, on this gym's sled, you did 240, 260 and 260. Tonight asks 260 across.
Nobody has read the leg extension machine at this gym, not once. Tonight's 105 and 135 are a deliberate baseline, not a prescription — log the pin you actually use.
Your recovery trainer capped the leg press at 200 on fatigue grounds and I upheld it. At this gym you have pressed 160 at most, on the high-foot version; 200 feet-low is already a step past that.

Two asks tonight sit above what you have actually done at this gym: the leg curl wants 145 for twelve where you managed ten on 5 September, and the calf press wants a third set of fifteen where you got thirteen. Both were flagged by your recovery trainer and both stand — if you come up short, that is information, not failure.
Bodyweight last logged 23 August at 207, twenty days ago and flat since 21 July. The show is 1 March.
Meso 2, week 3 of 4, a build block. Deload starts 21 September. Three trainers reported, no disagreements to settle, and no pain or injury objection.

Three Yes/No cards have been waiting since yesterday with no answer: drop the hanging leg raise from Legs A, rename the Push B opener to the dumbbell press you actually do, and drop the cable lateral raise from Push A.

proposals.why: Your two leg days run the same lifts from the fourth one on, so Legs A gives up the hanging leg raise and keeps the cable crunch while Legs B keeps both, which finally makes the two days different and takes tonight from 24 sets down to 22.

On 2 September you pressed dumbbells in this slot and wrote "New gym. No smith machine. Dumbbell press", so the Push B opener takes the name of the lift you are actually doing and asks for 4 sets of 8 to 10 instead of the smith bar's 6 to 8 — the name and the rep ask change, nothing else.

This has sat at the same 10 pounds since the middle of August without the reps ever climbing, and Push B already gives you three sets of dumbbell lateral raises, which is the lift you told us on 23 August you thought was getting too many sets for such a small muscle.

overrides.reason: The 180/220/240 here was read at the old gym on 20 August. At this gym you have pressed 160 at most, on the high-foot version on 5 September, and the same movement read about 20 lb under the old machine. You have not done this lift in 23 days. 140 is the feel-it set, 200 is the work. If 200 for ten is easy, say so and it moves next week.
Dumbbells weigh the same at both gyms, so 17.5 carries over honestly. Last time you got 9, 9 and 8 against an ask of ten, so the weight stays and the job is the reps. Weaker leg first, then match it.

This is the one lift the app already had right at this gym: 145 is a weight that does not even exist on the old machine's stack. Open at 130 and hold 145. You got 145 for ten on 5 September and this asks twelve, so the top sets are a real stretch; the fourth set is the new one, so ten is the target there.

Nobody has read this machine at this gym, so tonight is the reading. 105 to find it, then 135. Take fifteen with about two left in the tank and log the pin you actually used — that sets the real number next week instead of the old gym's 150.
Same reading at both gyms: 105 for twelve on 20 August and 105 for twelve again here on 5 September. Weight stays, the job is one more rep. Two sets of fifteen earns 112.5.
You finished 135 for fifteen on this machine on 5 September, which is the top of the range, so you have earned the next pin.

Do not load 300 — that is the old sled. On this one, on 5 September, you did 240 for fifteen, 260 for fifteen, then 260 for thirteen. 260 across tonight, and the third set of fifteen is the one you have not hit yet; three clean fifteens earns 280 next Legs A. Pause at the bottom, no bounce.
Cables did not change scale in the move and 65 is already your number here. You did 65 for ten three times on 5 September, the floor of the range, so stay at 65 and add a rep to the first two sets.
